svg.aria-label: Restaurant phone calls split into three endings and the products split with them. A call that ends in a message needs no integration at all: any general answering product handles hours, directions and taking a name, and the risk is that a caller who wanted to order gives up. A call that ends in a reservation needs write access to the booking platform, which means OpenTable, SevenRooms, Resy, Yelp or Tripleseat, and this is the tier where Slang AI publishes prices of three hundred and ninety nine dollars and five hundred and ninety nine dollars per location per month. A call that ends in a transaction needs write access to the point of sale, which means Toast, Square, Clover, SpotOn, Olo, PAR or NCR Aloha, and it must also handle modifiers, eighty-sixed items, quote times and payment; this is the tier where Loman, Incept AI and ConverseNow live and where nobody publishes a price. The rule underneath is that the hard part is never the voice, it is the write-back, and the further right you go the fewer vendors can do it and the less willing they are to name a number.
svg.text: Three ways a restaurant call can end — and the products split with them
Pick the ending you actually need before you compare voices. The voices are all fine. The write-back is where they differ.
Any general AI answering product does it
Risk: the caller who wanted to order hangs up
Write access to the booking platform:
Prices are published here — roughly $400–$600 per location
Write access to the POS: Toast, Square, Clover,
SpotOn, Olo, PAR, NCR Aloha — plus modifiers,
86’d items, a real quote time and payment
Nobody in this tier publishes a price
Figures are each vendor’s own published pricing as of August 2026. The further right you go, the fewer products can do it — and the less willing they are to name a number.
